Releases and compatibility

These guides describe Snurpo 1.5.0, published on 12 November 2026. Use the release page for downloads and checksums, or all releases for the full history.

What 1.5.0 adds#

Copy as cURL carries an effective captured request into a POSIX terminal. You preview it before copying; neither action sends traffic. Repeated headers and text or binary bodies are supported within the documented limits. Usage and boundaries.

The installed desktop app needs no Node runtime. Source tooling requires Node 26.13.1 or newer. The separate HAR comparison CLI keeps its own 0.1.0 version.

Download availability and validation#

TargetCurrent evidence
macOS Apple SiliconNative interaction has been exercised. Public ZIP is ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized.
Windows x64Installer available; CI build/package and headless MCP/capture coverage. Interactive use remains unverified.
Linux x64AppImage and Debian package available; CI build/package and headless MCP/capture coverage. Interactive use remains unverified.
Intel macOS / Linux arm64No package in the 1.5.0 release.
Android / FridaExperimental coverage for the specific setup described in the Android guide.

The gallery's existing native screenshots record 1.4.2. They are not screenshots of the 1.5.0 cURL feature. Detailed verification and dependency records retain their own dates and limits.

Scope became Snurpo in 1.4.2#

The name and mascot changed; saved-data and integration identifiers remain compatible. Existing sessions, CA trust and MCP configuration do not need a branding migration.

Keep existing scope.sqlite3, scope-ca.pem, scope-ca-key.pem, .scope.json, SCOPE_* variables and scope-mcp configurations. The certificate subject can still say Scope. Do not rename or remove these files merely to update the branding.

Quit old Scope before opening Snurpo: both use the same local archive and ports. Keep a backup of important work before changing installations. Historical releases and checksums remain unchanged.

On macOS, the mascot menu offers Show Snurpo and Quit Snurpo. Quit uses the application's cleanup path. This does not introduce automatic startup or change capture settings.

Read the migration reference for all retained compatibility names.
